name: Real-Time Image-Based Volume Lighting
definition: A two-step, GPU-friendly technique for real-time rendering of heterogeneous participating media under distant environment lighting. It estimates spherical scattered radiance at points in the medium, projects it into spherical harmonics (SH), and uses this information to compute single scattering via ray-marching. It requires no precomputation, supporting dynamic lighting, animated media, dynamic optical properties, emission, and self-shadowing.
